text:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel swap on staging I started seeing recurring OOMs during some long-chat load tests. Not a single big regression spike, more like fragmentation creeping up over time. cc @kevin @sara
kevin: Any profiler traces or p50/p95 numbers?
sara: I saw a few alerts from perf-bot too, maybe it already captured the trace?
perf-bot: automated: 2026-02-12T03:12Z - high kv-frag ratio detected on staging-cluster-3 (avg frag > 0.45)
maria: Uploading the quick summary: after kernel swap (v2.1.4 -> v2.2.0) decode throughput is neutral but long-tail memory footprint increases ~18% on 8k sessions. Reproducer attached below.
maria: Reproducer command: `./tools/run_workload.sh --profile --seed=42 --session-length=8000 --concurrency=12`
kevin: Interesting — could be kernel codegen packing different buffer sizes which increases slab fragmentation. Did you run the KV allocation heatmap?
maria: Yep, heatmap shows a steady increase in small free fragments and fewer >64KB free slots. Attached top-of-heap snapshot: most useful column is free-slot-size distribution.
sara: If large free slots disappear we end up forcing prefill to allocate new slices instead of reusing, which explains the slow growth. Two levers to consider: increase workspace headroom per engine, or change eviction to free larger contiguous slots earlier.
dave: Both have tradeoffs. Headroom reduces OOMs but wastes GPU RAM and can reduce concurrency. Evicting large slots earlier may increase decode tail latency for active sessions.
kevin: What about a hybrid: maintain a small soft-reserve for decode hot paths, but run periodic compaction/evicters that coalesce free fragments when fragmentation > threshold? That way we keep p50 low and avoid long-tail OOMs.
maria: I prototyped something: - workspace_headroom factor 1.2 -> 1.45 - per_request_prefill_cap lowered from 48MB -> 28MB - added a background coalescer pass every 15s when frag_ratio > 0.35
kevin: Nice. Any numbers?
maria: Quick benchmark on staging: baseline (post-swap) had average memory growth of +18% across 1h run and 6 OOMs per 1000 sessions. With the prototype hybrid: memory growth +6% and OOMs down to 1 per 1000. Throughput drop ~2.4% under peak concurrency (12).
sara: Those look promising. Did you try an alternative where we only use per-request caps without headroom change?
maria: Yes: cap-only reduces OOMs to 3/1000 but increases tail latency ~5% for long chats. Headroom + cap seems best single-step.
dave: Implementation complexity? Background coalescer might be tricky with current allocator lock scheme. Could we do an opportunistic coalesce during eviction to avoid heavy locking?
kevin: We should prefer lock-free bump coalesce: when scanning free list, try to merge adjacent slots using atomic CAS on slot headers. Fallback to queued compaction if CAS fails. Low-risk and avoids global pause.
maria: Patch landed in staging branch: diff summary below.
maria: ```
// allocator.h
float workspace_headroom = config->workspace_headroom_factor; // default 1.45 in staging
size_t per_request_prefill_cap = 28 * 1024 * 1024;
// coalescer: opportunistic CAS-based merge
```
kevin: Good. We need microbenchmarks for kernel selection too — maybe the kernel swap changed allocation alignment. Can we run a small kernel microbench that allocates 4KB, 8KB, 64KB buffers and measures alignment/stride distribution?
sara: I'll add a quick `alloc_stride_test` in perf-suite and run on staging nodes. Should help confirm whether new kernels prefer certain alignment.
maria: Ran alloc_stride_test on one node: v2.1.4 produced ~62% allocations aligned to 256B boundaries, v2.2.0 jumps to 78% aligned but with more fragmentation since larger alignment wastes smaller holes.
dave: That matches the hypothesis. Higher alignment granularity reduces usable small-slot packing. We can mitigate via allocator packing heuristics: prefer fit-first for small sizes, best-fit for larger.
kevin: Can we add a per-slab policy: small-slab uses tight packing (no alignment bump), large-slab keeps alignment. Add a fast-path that buckets allocations < 16KB into packed slabs.
maria: Implemented packed-slab fastpath in prototype; test results: fragmentation ratio drops from 0.46 -> 0.30 on the reproducer. Memory growth now ~+4% and OOMs ~0.5/1000.
sara: Where are we on rollout? Risks?
dave: Risks: race conditions in opportunistic coalescer and packed-slab codepaths. Also potential perf regression on short, latency-sensitive requests due to extra checks in allocation path. Need canary.
kevin: Proposed rollout plan: 1) Keep kernel v2.2.0 on staging with hybrid allocator flags off. 2) Canary flags on 5% of dedicated capacity with `alloc_packed_slab=true` and `workspace_headroom=1.45`. 3) Monitor kv-frag, OOMs, p95 latency for 24h. 4) If stable -> 25% -> 100% with auto rollback if OOMs increase by >2x.
maria: I'll prepare a short watchlist in console: kv-frag, free-slot-dist, decode-tail-latency, OOM-rate, GPU-util. Also add perfbot alert if frag_ratio > 0.4.
kevin: One more thing — eval metrics. We should run end-to-end quality evals to ensure packed-slab doesn't change determinism or tokenization boundary behavior (shouldn't, but safety check).
sara: Agreed. Running eval harness now on a 5000-chat prompt set.
perf-bot: automated: eval run started 2026-02-12T05:08Z, harness id=ev-7362
maria: Thanks all. I'll push the canary config change and tag @oncall if we see >1 OOM / 100 sessions in canary. Follow-ups: if coalescer lock-free path has issues, fallback plan is to increase workspace headroom and keep packed-slab only.
kevin: Great work. Please paste the canary config here once pushed. Also add a short note in eng-runtime channel about the root cause hypothesis (kernel-alignment -> slab waste) so infra folks are aware.
sara: Canary config pasted to staging-ops: `alloc_packed_slab=true;workspace_headroom=1.45;per_request_prefill_cap=28MB;coalesce_interval_s=15;frag_threshold=0.35`
dave: I'll review the CAS logic for coalescer this afternoon. If all good, we can start canary in 30m. :thumbsup:
maria: Starting canary now. Will update thread with first 1h metrics.
perf-bot: automated: canary started on staging-group-alpha at 2026-02-12T05:41Z
kevin: Thanks — ping me if any spikes.
